title: Federal Judge: US Marshals Lack Legal Authority and Training for ICE Courthouse Arrests
excerpt: U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth ruled that U.S. Marshals assigned to D.C. Superior Court lacked both legal authority and the immigration training required by federal regulations to make civil immigration arrests. The court found the government failed to show that an online briefing provided to Marshals was 'substantially equivalent' to required immigration law enforcement training.
content:
On July 22, 2026, U.S. District Judge Royce C. Lamberth refused to dismiss a class-action lawsuit challenging immigration arrests made by U.S. Marshals in D.C. Superior Court, ruling the Marshals lacked both authority and the necessary training for such arrests.

The court found the government failed to demonstrate that Marshals had received the immigration training required by federal regulations. Marshals assigned to D.C. Superior Court received only virtual instruction from ICE attorneys covering civil immigration authorities, but the government could not show this was "substantially equivalent" to the immigration law enforcement courses referenced in federal regulations.

  • Judge Lamberth held that a 2025 executive order "did not successfully amend the regulation and cannot constitute a legitimate delegation of authority" to U.S. Marshals to make civil immigration arrests.
  • The ruling found the administration had effectively changed federal regulations without the notice-and-comment rulemaking process required under the Administrative Procedure Act.
  • The decision is part of a broader wave of federal court rulings finding ICE and allied agency arrest practices unlawful due to inadequate training and procedural failures.
